question: Which source blockers can a person shift that this factory cannot?
answer: 232 human-action item(s). The top 20 could unlock 67 famil(ies) and close 149 source obligation(s).
whyThisIsShort: 256 families are SOURCE_BLOCKED and most of that is internal work. Only a named form with no held bytes is something a person can fetch; a family that names no document at all is discovery work, not an errand.
noContactIsInvented: This repository holds no phone number or email address for any court or agency. Every contact channel is marked REQUIRES_LOOKUP rather than filled with a plausible address, because a fabricated contact is acted on precisely because it looks complete.

INTERNAL_SOURCE_WORK_NOT_FOR_ROGER.rule: Roger is not asked to perform repository, hashing, mapping or promotion work. If an item below would have him touch this repository, it is misfiled.

categories.what: computing or comparing SHA-256 of a held or fetched binary
moving bytes into governed custody and writing the custody record
indexing the Master Library and reconciling the corpus index against held bytes
mapping a route or family to the documents it requires
regenerating the queue, the manifest, the conveyor or the collision record
deciding which lane owns which path and resolving collisions
any question of what the law requires
generators, verifiers, workflows, prompts and their tests

INTERNAL_SOURCE_WORK_NOT_FOR_ROGER.excludedFromTheRankedList: 104 SOURCE_BLOCKED famil(ies) name no official form at all. Those are DISC discovery obligations -- settling which document a route requires -- and they are lane work, not an errand.

statutoryCitationsMisqueuedAsForms.why: These are statutory citations, not published forms. There is no PDF at the other end and no clerk who can hand one over; the routes need a custom pleading drafted against the statute. Ranked on a fetch list they would send a person to several offices to ask for something that does not exist.
statutoryCitationsMisqueuedAsForms.owner: a packet-build lane, as custom-pleading drafting — not Roger, and not an ACQ lane

whoOwnsEachStepAfterRogerReturnsBytes: ACQ lane: record the file and its SHA-256, MIME, page count, technology and byte size
PROMO lane: verify the receipt, compare the hash, create the custody record
Captain: regenerate the queue and release the newly source-ready families

rankingCriteriaInOrder: likelihood a clerk or agency can provide the source quickly
current official form number already known
official host currently blocking automated access

Subject: current official edition of Statement of Inability to Afford Payment of Court Costs or an Appeal Bond (TX)

Good morning —

I am looking for the current official edition of Statement of Inability to Afford Payment of Court Costs or an Appeal Bond, used for record clearing petitions in TX.

Three questions, and I am happy to be pointed at a page rather than sent a file:

  1. Is this still the form the court accepts, or has it been superseded?
  2. Where is the current edition published?
  3. Is the statewide edition the one this court uses, or does this court use its own?

Thank you for your time.

— Roger Roman, LegalEase
